note: The 4.8 build is a Python agent using the Anthropic SDK in code, not an n8n workflow; the full agent.py is in PART 4 · Solved problem, step "Write agent.py".

walk.title: Build it: a terminal agent with two tools
walk.sample: You: How much is tatashe today? · You: Where is HL-0042?

steps.say: We start with a project folder and a virtual environment, so this project's packages stay separate from everything else.
Create the API key in the Claude Console, set a monthly spend limit first, then put the key in the environment. Never type it into the code.
In agent.py, the client reads the key from the environment by itself. Sample prices and one order live in the file for now.
The tools are plain Python functions that return small dictionaries. If a product isn't found, get_price says so and offers suggestions, so the model never has to guess.
show: def get_price(product) → found, name, unit, price, stock
def get_order_status(order_id) → found, status, rider, eta

steps.say: Each tool is described to the model with a name, a description and an input schema, the same rules as in n8n. Both tools only read. There's no tool to change an order.
The system message says: only state prices and order details from your tools, and if a tool errors, apologise and say Tolu will follow up.
show: Only state prices and order details that come from your tools.

steps.say: Here's the loop. Send the messages, and if the model asks for a tool, append its request first, then send back each result with the matching tool use ID.
A tool that fails doesn't crash the program. The error goes back to the model as a message marked is_error, so the agent can apologise.
And the hard stop: at most six turns, just like Max Iterations in n8n. If it runs out, the customer gets a polite fallback.
show: return "Sorry, I couldn't finish that. Tolu will follow up…"

steps.say: Run it and ask about tatashe. The arrow line in the terminal is your trace: you can see exactly which tool was called, with what input.
steps.data: Tatashe pepper · ₦9,000 · big bag · 6 in stock

steps.say: Then ask where HL-0042 is. Your wording will differ, but the tool call and the facts should match.
steps.data: Out for delivery · Musa · before 2 p.m.

steps.say: Now prove the safety nets. Make get_price raise a connection error: the agent apologises and the program keeps running.
Ask, do you have yam? The tool returns found false with suggestions, and the agent asks instead of inventing.
Finally set max turns to one and ask a two-part question. You get the polite fallback, not an endless loop.

walk.end: About sixty lines, two read-only tools, no crashes when a tool fails, and a loop that always ends.
